standard_prerequisites.name: m-covered family
standard_prerequisites.statement: The family is m-covered when all its members are contained in a single coset determined by prescribing m images.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the conclusion of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Minimal certificate
standard_prerequisites.statement: A certificate of the member that is minimal for the given function, so its size is the value of the certificate-size function at that member.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the coset whose size is estimated.

standard_prerequisites.name: Intersection bound for representatives
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two members with equal characteristic value admit representatives meeting exactly in the intersection of their certificates.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the estimate that forces the second member into the coset.

core_obligations: Take a minimal certificate for the given member and consider the coset it determines, prescribing one fewer image than the certificate has (source line 574).
For another member of the family, use the representative lemma to obtain a representative whose certificate meets the first one in exactly the intersection of the two certificates (source line 576).
Conclude that the second member lies in the coset determined by the first certificate with one image dropped, which is the covering statement (source line 576).

proof_roadmap.step: Choose a minimal certificate and the coset it determines.
Apply the representative lemma and read off the covering.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 568-572: for the characteristic function of a 2-intersecting family of permutations with common certificate size at most n minus two, each member implies that the whole family is covered by the coset determined by a minimal certificate for that member with one image fewer. The proof (source lines 573-577) takes a minimal certificate for the chosen member, forms the coset it determines with one image dropped, and then, for any other member of the family, invokes the representative lemma to find a representative whose certificate meets the first in exactly the intersection of the two; that intersection bound is precisely what forces the member into the coset. The statement records the covering and neither the choice of coset nor the use of the representative lemma.
